Alexander Heidel, The Gilgamesh Epic and Old Testament Parallels (1946; 2nd ed. 1949)

  • Author: Alexander Heidel (1907–1955), Oriental Institute, University of Chicago
  • Publisher: University of Chicago Press, 1946; 2nd ed. 1949 (Phoenix pbk reprints 1963 ff., still sold by UChicago Press)
  • Source used: Faded Page (Distributed Proofreaders Canada) e-text, book #20220136: https://www.fadedpage.com/showbook.php?pid=20220136 (HTML: …/books/20220136/html.php; PDF via link.php?file=20220136-a5.pdf). The transcription follows the 1949 2nd edition, with a 1946 first-publication note.
  • Retrieved: 2026-10-16
  • License / copyright: Faded Page states it is public domain in Canada, "may be under copyright in some countries". Heidel died in 1955, so it is also PD in life+70 jurisdictions, including Israel and the EU, from 1 Jan 2026. US status is unclear: it depends on whether the copyright was renewed. HathiTrust (which would tell us) could not be checked because of a Cloudflare block. Every archive.org copy is lending-only except one patron upload, which was not used. Fine for private research here; do not redistribute in the US without checking.

Files

  • fadedpage-20220136.raw.html: the full DP-Canada HTML e-book (UTF-8, with footnotes).
  • fadedpage-20220136-a5.pdf: DP-Canada's A5 PDF of the same text (2 MB).
  • fadedpage-showbook-20220136.raw.html: catalogue page with the PD statement.
  • full-book.md: clean extraction of the whole book.
  • tablet-XI.md: Tablet XI (Heidel's ll. 1–308 + colophon 309–311) with its footnotes [164]–[217] appended.
  • chapter-II--other-flood-versions.md: Sumerian Deluge (Nippur), Atrahasis fragments, Berossus, with footnotes.
  • chapter-IV--OT-parallels-flood.md: Chapter IV, "Old Testament Parallels" on the Flood. A point-by-point comparison with Genesis 6–9: authors and reason of the flood, the hero, the announcement, the ark, its occupants, the date, causes, duration, landing place, bird scene, exit, sacrifice, blessings, covenant, and the question of dependence.

Line numbering

Heidel numbers every line, following Thompson 1930. Compared with George (eBL):

  • Identical or ±1 up to ~140. Puzur-Amurri: Heidel 94 vs George 95.
  • Dove: Heidel 146 vs George 148. Flies: Heidel 161 vs George 163. Lapis: Heidel 164 vs George 165–166.
  • "Hitherto Utnapishtim has been but a man": Heidel 193 vs George 203. "Mouth of the rivers": Heidel 195–196 vs George 205–206.
  • The end: Heidel 307 (+308 catch-line "pukku") vs George 328 (+catch-line).

Align by content, not number. Note the OCR-type slip "ll." for "11." in line 11.

Assessment

Very valuable for this project. It is a careful, literal translation made for the Chicago Assyrian Dictionary files, with parentheses marking explanatory additions, square brackets marking restorations, and "(?)" marking uncertain readings. It is also the classic, conservative comparison with Genesis. Outdated in: pre-1950 readings (Nisir for Nimuš, Puzur-Amurri, "Irragal"), no Assur, Babylon or Nimrud manuscripts, and older views on Atrahasis (before Lambert–Millard 1969). Register: mid-20th-c. scholarly English with "thou/thee" for speech.
